discovery_note: The four captured John 1:1 named searches are bounded candidate probes. P66, P75, and 01 are reviewed here; 02 remains unreviewed. Discovery is incomplete.

witnesses.classification_citation: CSNTM, Manuscript P66, https://manuscripts.csntm.org/Manuscript/Group/GA_P66_Bodmer, manuscript details: Greek papyrus, shelf P. Bodmer II; consulted 2026-10-01.
witnesses.identity_citation: CSNTM, Manuscript P66, https://manuscripts.csntm.org/Manuscript/Group/GA_P66_Bodmer; IGNTP, A Transcription of John in P66, TEI title with document key 10066, https://epapers.bham.ac.uk/id/eprint/1759/10/04_P66.xml; consulted 2026-10-01.
witnesses.coverage_citation: International Greek New Testament Project, A Transcription of John in P66, version 2.1 (2013), TEI page P1, column 1, lines 2–8, verse elements B04K1V1–B04K1V5, https://epapers.bham.ac.uk/id/eprint/1759/10/04_P66.xml; repository record https://epapers.bham.ac.uk/id/eprint/1759/; consulted 2026-10-01.
witnesses.coverage_reason: The IGNTP transcription records surviving Greek in each of John 1:1–5 on its first page. Some letters are supplied as lost or illegible, so the positive status is partial. The NTVMR page 10 entries are index links, not the physical proof.
witnesses.unit_label: Original writing on the opening page of P66
witnesses.unit_citation: IGNTP, A Transcription of John in P66, version 2.1 (2013), page P1, column 1, lines 2–8, https://epapers.bham.ac.uk/id/eprint/1759/10/04_P66.xml; the cited verse elements have base transcription outside correction readings.
witnesses.unit_reason: The recorded positive text is the opening page's original copying; no separate correction reading is used for these five verse reviews.

assessments.citation: CSNTM, Manuscript P66, date field '2nd-3rd Century', https://manuscripts.csntm.org/Manuscript/Group/GA_P66_Bodmer; consulted 2026-10-01. Bounds 101–300 CE cover the two complete centuries; this catalogue range is conditional, not a documented consensus.

assessments.original_notation: Late second or early third century
assessments.citation: CSNTM, Manuscript P66, description, https://manuscripts.csntm.org/Manuscript/Group/GA_P66_Bodmer; consulted 2026-10-01. 'Late' and 'early' have no stated numeric bounds, so no interval is inferred.

witnesses.classification_citation: Vatican Apostolic Library, The Hanna Papyrus 1 (Mater Verbi), https://www.vaticanlibrary.va/en/multimedia/papiro-hanna-1.html; identifies P75 as a Greek Gospel papyrus; consulted 2026-10-01.
witnesses.identity_citation: Vatican Apostolic Library, The Hanna Papyrus 1 (Mater Verbi), https://www.vaticanlibrary.va/en/multimedia/papiro-hanna-1.html; CSNTM, Manuscript P75, https://manuscripts.csntm.org/manuscript/Group/GA_P75; consulted 2026-10-01.
witnesses.coverage_citation: Vatican Apostolic Library, A Venerable Witness of the Gospels of Luke and John: Bodmer Papyrus XIV-XV (P75), PDF p. 3, transcription of John 1:1–5 on folio 2A8r, https://www.vaticanlibrary.va/moduli/BodmerFarina_ing.pdf; library manuscript description https://www.vaticanlibrary.va/en/multimedia/papiro-hanna-1.html; consulted 2026-10-01.
witnesses.coverage_reason: The Vatican Library publishes a verse-marked transcription of the surviving John prologue leaf containing each of John 1:1–5. The status is conservatively partial; the NTVMR page 620 row is a matching index link.
witnesses.unit_label: Main writing on the P75 John prologue leaf
witnesses.unit_citation: Vatican Apostolic Library, A Venerable Witness of the Gospels of Luke and John, PDF p. 3, John 1:1–5 transcription and folio 2A8r, https://www.vaticanlibrary.va/moduli/BodmerFarina_ing.pdf; consulted 2026-10-01.
witnesses.unit_reason: The reviewed verse material belongs to the main writing on the cited prologue leaf; this review does not date or count any separate correction.

assessments.citation: CSNTM, Manuscript P75, date field '3rd Century', https://manuscripts.csntm.org/manuscript/Group/GA_P75; consulted 2026-10-01. Bounds 201–300 CE represent the complete century and remain a conditional catalogue assessment.

Vatican Apostolic Library, The Hanna Papyrus 1 (Mater Verbi), https://www.vaticanlibrary.va/en/multimedia/papiro-hanna-1.html; consulted 2026-10-01. 'Early' has no stated numeric bounds, so this observation is not normalized for ranking.

witnesses.classification_citation: Codex Sinaiticus Project, See the Manuscript, John 1, https://www.codexsinaiticus.org/en/manuscript.aspx?book=36&chapter=1; Greek manuscript folio 247; consulted 2026-10-01.
witnesses.identity_citation: Codex Sinaiticus Project, See the Manuscript, John 1, https://www.codexsinaiticus.org/en/manuscript.aspx?book=36&chapter=1; CSNTM, Manuscript GA 01, https://manuscripts.csntm.org/manuscript/Group/GA_01; consulted 2026-10-01.
witnesses.coverage_citation: Codex Sinaiticus Project, See the Manuscript, John 1, folio 247, scribe A, verse-by-verse Greek transcription for John 1:1–5, https://www.codexsinaiticus.org/en/manuscript.aspx?book=36&chapter=1; consulted 2026-10-01.
witnesses.coverage_reason: The manuscript project's folio 247 transcription explicitly prints the Greek text under verse markers 1:1–5. The positive status is conservatively partial. NTVMR page 950 supplies the corresponding index entries.
witnesses.unit_label: Scribe A on the John 1 folio
witnesses.unit_citation: Codex Sinaiticus Project, See the Manuscript, John 1, folio 247 labelled scribe A, https://www.codexsinaiticus.org/en/manuscript.aspx?book=36&chapter=1; consulted 2026-10-01.
witnesses.unit_reason: The cited folio identifies scribe A for the transcribed John 1:1–5 text; no later correction is counted in these verse reviews.

assessments.citation: Codex Sinaiticus Project, Date, https://www.codexsinaiticus.org/en/codex/date.aspx; consulted 2026-10-01. The project says the codex is generally dated to the fourth century. Bounds 301–400 CE represent that complete century; applicability to scribe A is conditional in this prototype.

Codex Sinaiticus Project, Date, https://www.codexsinaiticus.org/en/codex/date.aspx; consulted 2026-10-01. The project notes this more precise description sometimes appears; 'middle' has no stated inclusive bounds.
